content: Horatio Spafford put his wife and four daughters on a ship to Europe, planning to follow. The ship sank, and only his wife survived. Sailing over the very waters where his girls were lost, he wrote It Is Well with My Soul. God's peace can hold a heart that the sea has broken.

After the shipwreck that took her four daughters, Anna Spafford was pulled from the water and sent her husband a short telegram that began, saved alone. Years later the couple moved to Jerusalem and served the poor there. The Lord gives grieving people a new work of mercy to do.

Fanny Crosby lost her sight as a baby after a bad medical treatment. She never held it against anyone. She once said that blindness might be a blessing, because the first face she would ever see would be her Savior's. She wrote thousands of hymns. God can turn a lifelong darkness into song.

One day Fanny Crosby's friend Phoebe Knapp played her a new melody on the piano and asked what it said. Fanny answered almost at once with the words Blessed Assurance, Jesus is mine. That hymn has comforted believers ever since. God often gives His best gifts in a quiet, ordinary moment.

Joseph Scriven's bride to be drowned the night before their wedding in Ireland. Years later, living in Canada, he heard his mother was ill far away and wrote her a simple poem about prayer. It became What a Friend We Have in Jesus. Christ is the friend who stays when every other comfort is gone.

Joseph Scriven spent his later years in Ontario quietly helping widows and the poor, even cutting firewood for those who could not pay. Few people knew he had written a famous hymn. A humble life of service can sing of Jesus as loudly as any choir. God sees the hidden kindnesses.

Thomas Chisholm was an ordinary man, a teacher, an editor, and later an insurance agent, often in poor health. He said there was no dramatic story behind Great Is Thy Faithfulness, only a morning by morning awareness of God's care. The Lord's faithfulness shows up in plain, everyday mornings.

In nineteen thirty two, Thomas Dorsey's wife Nettie died giving birth, and their baby son died soon after. Crushed, Dorsey sat at a piano with a friend, and out came Precious Lord, Take My Hand. The Lord leads His children through the storm and into the light, even when they can barely stand.

Bill and Gloria Gaither were expecting a baby during a troubled, uneasy time in the country, and fear crept in. When their son Benjy was born, peace returned, and they wrote Because He Lives. Because Jesus is alive, a parent can face tomorrow, and so can you. God rules every tomorrow.

Bill Gaither was a high school English teacher in Indiana when he met Gloria, a fellow teacher at the same school. They married, and together they wrote hundreds of gospel songs. God can take a couple of ordinary schoolteachers and use them to bless millions. He wastes nothing.

In nineteen sixty three, Bill Gaither was moved by an old phrase about the touch of the Lord and wrote He Touched Me. It became one of the most recorded gospel songs of its time. One gentle touch from Jesus can make a whole life new. The Lord still reaches out to the weary tonight.

Around nineteen ninety one, after a recording session, Bill Gaither invited older gospel singers to stay and sing around the piano. Tears flowed as old friends sang the songs of their youth. That evening grew into the Homecoming gatherings. God loves to gather His family together in song.

Carl Boberg, a young Swedish man, was walking home when a sudden thunderstorm rolled in, then cleared over a calm bay. Hearing church bells and birdsong afterward, he wrote a poem that became How Great Thou Art. The God of thunder is also the God of quiet evenings. He is great in both.

Stuart Hine, an English missionary, learned the Russian version of a Swedish hymn while serving in Eastern Europe. Out in the mountains, under the stars and among the people, he added his own verses in English. We sing them as How Great Thou Art. God's praise crosses every border.

Civilla Martin and her husband visited a couple who had been sick and confined for years. Asked how they stayed so hopeful, the wife pointed to God's care for the sparrow. Civilla wrote His Eye Is on the Sparrow. If the Father watches the smallest bird, He is watching over you.

Annie Johnson Flint was orphaned young and later crippled by arthritis so severe she could barely hold a pen. Still she wrote poems like He Giveth More Grace, about God's strength growing as our burdens grow. When our own strength runs out, the Lord's supply is only beginning.

Charlotte Elliott was an invalid who felt useless while her family worked hard to raise money for a school. Alone at home, she wrote Just As I Am, about coming to Christ with nothing to offer. That hymn led countless people to faith. God welcomes us before we have anything to bring.

Frances Havergal once stayed in a house with ten people, some not believers and some unhappy believers. She prayed for every one of them, and before she left, all were blessed. That night, too joyful to sleep, she wrote Take My Life and Let It Be. God answers the prayers of a willing heart.

George Matheson lost most of his sight as a young man. On the evening of his sister's wedding, alone and carrying an old sorrow, he wrote O Love That Wilt Not Let Me Go in just a few minutes. The love of God does not let go, even when human love does. It holds on through every loss.

Henry Francis Lyte was a pastor in a fishing village in England, weak with lung disease. Near the end of his life he preached a farewell sermon and soon after gave his family the hymn Abide with Me. He died not long after. As evening falls, the Lord abides with those who ask Him to stay.

Lina Sandell was on a boat on a Swedish lake with her father when he fell overboard and drowned before her eyes. Out of that sorrow came hymns of quiet trust, among them Day by Day. The Father who gives strength for each day gives it again tomorrow. His grace comes in daily portions.

Philip Bliss was a beloved gospel songwriter. In eighteen seventy six, a train he and his wife were riding crashed through a bridge in Ohio. He survived the fall but went back into the burning wreck to find her, and both died. Love like that reflects the God who came looking for us.

Ira Sankey, D. L. Moody's song leader, found a poem in a newspaper on a train in Scotland. At a meeting in Edinburgh, Moody suddenly asked him to sing. Sankey set the poem The Ninety and Nine to a tune as he went. The Good Shepherd still goes out into the night for the one lost sheep.

Cleland McAfee was a pastor whose two young nieces died of diphtheria within a short time. Grieving with his brother's family, he wrote Near to the Heart of God, about a place of rest and comfort. In the hardest seasons, the safest place is close to the Father's heart.

Adelaide Pollard longed to go to Africa as a missionary but could not raise the money. Discouraged, she went to a prayer meeting and heard an older woman simply ask the Lord to have His own way. She went home and wrote Have Thine Own Way, Lord. God shapes us best when we rest in His hands.

Louisa Stead lost her husband when he drowned off Long Island while trying to save a child. Left with a young daughter and very little money, she wrote Tis So Sweet to Trust in Jesus. Later she served as a missionary in Africa. The Lord proves Himself trustworthy in the poorest days.

Charles Tindley, the son of an enslaved father, taught himself to read and worked as a janitor at a church in Philadelphia. Years later he returned to that same church as its pastor, and wrote songs like Stand By Me. God lifts the humble and stands beside them in every storm.

Albert Brumley was picking cotton on his family's farm in Oklahoma, humming an old song about flying away. The idea stayed with him for a few years until it became I'll Fly Away. That song has carried tired hearts toward heaven ever since. God plants hope even in a hot cotton field.

Elizabeth Prentiss lost two of her young children within a short time. In deep grief she wrote More Love to Christ, asking that her sorrow would draw her closer to the Lord rather than away. Her prayer was answered. God can use even our tears to deepen our love for Him.

Edward Mote was a cabinetmaker in London who came to faith as a young man. One morning on his way to work the words of a hymn came to him about building life on the solid rock of Christ. It became My Hope Is Built on Nothing Less. When all around gives way, Jesus is firm ground.

As a teenager, Isaac Watts complained that the hymns sung in his church were dull. His father told him, in effect, to write better ones. He did, writing hundreds, including Joy to the World and When I Survey the Wondrous Cross. God can use a young person's restless heart for lasting good.

Charles Wesley came to a living faith in May of seventeen thirty eight, a few days before his brother John. Soon after, he wrote And Can It Be, marveling that Christ would die for him. He went on to write thousands of hymns. A heart set free by grace cannot help but sing.

William Cowper battled deep depression for much of his life. His friend, the pastor John Newton, walked with him, and together they wrote the Olney Hymns. Cowper wrote God Moves in a Mysterious Way. Even when the mind is clouded, God's purposes are ripening quietly behind the frowning clouds.

Robert Robinson was a rough young man in London who went to mock the preacher George Whitefield. Instead, the message stayed with him for years until he gave his life to Christ. Later he wrote Come Thou Fount of Every Blessing. God keeps pursuing hearts that are prone to wander.

Martin Rinkart was a pastor in a walled German town during war and a terrible plague. He conducted thousands of funerals, including his wife's. Yet in those years he wrote Now Thank We All Our God. Gratitude that grows in the darkest years is a gift that only God can give.

Maltbie Babcock was a pastor in New York who loved to walk early in the morning to a hill overlooking the countryside and Lake Ontario. He would say he was going out to see his Father's world. His poem became This Is My Father's World. All creation quietly declares whose world it is.

Annie Hawks was a busy mother doing her housework one bright morning in Brooklyn when a deep sense of needing the Lord came over her. She wrote I Need Thee Every Hour. Her pastor, Robert Lowry, set it to music. God meets us not only in crisis but in every ordinary hour.

Anna Warner and her sister wrote stories together in New York. In one of their novels, a character comforts a dying child with a simple poem that begins Jesus loves me, this I know. Children around the world have sung it since. The deepest truth about God is simple enough for a child.

William Featherston was only a teenager in Montreal when he wrote the words of My Jesus, I Love Thee. He died young, but his simple poem of devotion is still sung. A young heart's sincere love for Christ can outlive the singer. God treasures the devotion of the young.

George Frideric Handel wrote the music for Messiah in only a few weeks in seventeen forty one. Its first performance in Dublin raised money for prisoners and the sick. Ever since, choirs have sung the whole gospel story through it. God can make a single season of work bless the centuries.

Johann Sebastian Bach often wrote the letters for Jesus help at the top of a page of music and for to God alone be glory at the end. He worked as a church musician, raising a large family and burying several children. Faithful daily work done for God becomes an offering of praise.

Thomas Ken, a seventeenth century English bishop, wrote morning and evening hymns for students at Winchester. The last verse of each became the Doxology, praise God from whom all blessings flow. People still sing it at bedtime and at table. Every blessing, day and night, flows from Him.

George Beverly Shea found a poem by Rhea Miller that his mother had left on the family piano. It was I'd Rather Have Jesus. He sat down and wrote a melody for it that same day as a young man. He sang it for decades. A mother's quiet nudge can shape a whole life for God.

For decades George Beverly Shea sang at Billy Graham's crusades, often just before the message. He sang How Great Thou Art so many times that it became beloved across America. He lived past a hundred years old. God can use one steady, faithful voice for a very long time.

Stuart Hamblen was a popular cowboy singer and radio host who struggled with drinking. In nineteen forty nine he went to Billy Graham's tent meetings in Los Angeles and gave his life to Christ. Later he wrote It Is No Secret What God Can Do. What the Lord does for one, He will do for others.

Ethel Waters grew up in deep poverty in Pennsylvania and became a famous singer and actress. Later in life she traveled with Billy Graham's crusades, singing His Eye Is on the Sparrow. She often said she knew God loved her. The Father's care reaches every child, however hard the beginning.

Mahalia Jackson grew up singing in a New Orleans church. When she became famous, she was offered money to sing popular secular songs but held to gospel music. She sang about the Lord on the world's biggest stages. God honors those who sing His praise with their whole heart.

Dottie Rambo began writing songs as a little girl sitting by a creek in Kentucky. She went on to write hundreds of gospel songs, including We Shall Behold Him. Even in years of pain from a back injury, she kept writing. God gives songs in the night to those who keep listening.

Keith Green came from a Jewish family and searched for truth as a young musician in California. In the early seventies he and his wife Melody came to faith in Jesus. They opened their home to people in need, from runaways to addicts. A changed heart quickly becomes an open door.

Keith Green later offered his music on a pay what you can basis, sending albums to many who could not pay. In nineteen eighty two he died in a small plane crash along with two of his children. Melody carried on the ministry. God sustains the grieving, and His work goes on.

Phil Keaggy lost part of a finger in a farm accident as a small boy, yet grew into one of the finest guitarists of his time. When his mother died after a car crash in nineteen seventy, his sister pointed him to Jesus, and he believed. God brings new life even out of a family's deepest loss.

Rich Mullins wrote Awesome God and Hold Me Jesus. Though his songs did well, he lived simply, taking a modest salary and giving much of the rest away. In his last years he taught music to children on a Navajo reservation. The Lord delights in a heart that holds things loosely and loves freely.

Steve Green grew up as the son of missionaries in Argentina, where he learned to love both the gospel and music. He became a beloved voice of the eighties and nineties, singing songs like People Need the Lord. A childhood spent among missionaries can grow into a lifetime of ministry.

Twila Paris grew up in a family devoted to missions and began singing in church as a little girl. She later wrote worship songs like We Will Glorify and He Is Exalted, sung in churches everywhere. When a young heart is offered to God, He can make it a voice of worship for many.

Michael Card studied the Bible in college under a teacher who encouraged him to write songs about what he was learning. Songs like El Shaddai came from that study. He has spent his life setting scripture to music. When we dig deeply into God's Word, it begins to sing in us.

Don Moen's wife's sister and her husband were in a car accident on the way to a ski trip, and their young son Jeremy was killed. Flying to be with them, Don was given a song from Isaiah, and he sang it to them after the funeral. It was God Will Make a Way. The Lord makes paths in the wilderness.

In the early eighties, Michael W. Smith and his wife Debbie wrote Friends as a farewell for a friend moving away. It became a song sung at graduations and goodbyes for years. Christian friendships do not really end. In Christ, friends are friends forever, and God keeps them in His hand.

After losing both their parents within about two years, Matthew and Nelly Ward went to live with their older sister Annie and her husband. The three siblings began singing together as Second Chapter of Acts. God sets the lonely in families and gives them a song to share.

Annie Herring of Second Chapter of Acts wrote Easter Song, a bright song about the risen Lord, which became one of the best loved songs of early Christian music. She had walked through the loss of both parents. Resurrection hope shines brightest where sorrow has been real.

Barry McGuire was famous in the sixties for a gloomy protest song. Searching for meaning, he came to faith in Jesus in the early seventies and began singing gospel songs instead. God can change a voice that sang about the end of the world into one that sings about a new beginning.

Noel Paul Stookey of the folk trio Peter, Paul and Mary came to faith in Christ around the end of the sixties. Soon after, he wrote The Wedding Song for a friend's wedding and gave its earnings to charity. When Jesus enters a life, generosity often follows close behind.

Cliff Richard was one of Britain's biggest pop stars when he came to faith in Christ in the mid sixties. He spoke of his faith publicly at a Billy Graham meeting in London and kept singing for decades. God can reach a person at the very top of the charts and give real peace.

Chuck Smith pastored a small church in Costa Mesa, California, in the late sixties when young hippies began showing up barefoot. Instead of turning them away, the church welcomed them. Many came to faith and began writing new songs of worship. God loves to surprise a church with new people.

The band Love Song was a group of young musicians searching for truth in California who came to faith at Calvary Chapel around nineteen seventy. Their gentle songs helped begin a new era of Christian music. God can turn spiritual seekers into singers of His grace.

Kurt Kaiser wrote Pass It On around nineteen sixty nine for a youth retreat, about how a small spark can get a fire going. Young people sang it around campfires for decades. The love of God spreads like that, one person telling another. Small sparks of faith become a warm glow.

John W. Peterson flew dangerous transport flights over the mountains between India and China during the Second World War. After the war he wrote hundreds of gospel songs, including It Took a Miracle, about the God who hung the stars. The Creator of the heavens is the One who saves.

Ron Hamilton lost an eye to cancer as a young man. During that hard season he wrote Rejoice in the Lord, a song about trusting God's plan even when we cannot see it. He later created the Patch the Pirate stories for children. God can turn a painful loss into joy for many.

Billy Graham was a sixteen year old farm boy in North Carolina when he went to a revival meeting in Charlotte and gave his life to Christ. He went on to preach to millions around the world. God sees the teenager in the back row and knows what He will do with that life.

In nineteen forty nine, Billy Graham was troubled by doubts about the Bible. At a conference center in the San Bernardino mountains, he walked into the woods, set his Bible on a tree stump, and told God he would accept it by faith. Weeks later the Los Angeles crusade began. God honors simple trust.

Ruth Bell Graham grew up in China as the daughter of a missionary doctor. Married to Billy Graham, she raised their five children while he traveled, often praying alone through long nights. Her poems speak of quiet trust. God strengthens the faithful ones who serve behind the scenes.

Louis Zamperini survived weeks adrift on a raft and years in brutal prison camps during the war. Afterward he was haunted by nightmares and anger. In nineteen forty nine he went to a Billy Graham meeting in Los Angeles and came to Christ. He later forgave many of his captors. God heals the deepest wounds.

Joni Eareckson was seventeen when she dove into shallow water in the Chesapeake Bay and was paralyzed. After years of anger and despair, she found that God's grace was enough. She learned to paint holding a brush in her mouth, and began a ministry for people with disabilities. God's strength shines in weakness.

Joni Eareckson Tada later faced breast cancer and chronic pain on top of decades in a wheelchair. She has said that she would rather be in this chair knowing Jesus than on her feet without Him. Her life shows that God's nearness is a treasure worth more than easy days.

Eric Liddell refused to run the hundred meters at the nineteen twenty four Olympics because the race was held on a Sunday. Instead he ran the four hundred, a race he was not expected to win, and won the gold. God honors those who quietly honor Him, whatever the outcome.

After his Olympic victory, Eric Liddell went to China as a missionary teacher. During the war he was held in a Japanese internment camp, where he taught children and helped the elderly. He died there in nineteen forty five. A life given away for Christ is never wasted.

Brother Andrew, a young Dutchman, carried Bibles into countries where they were forbidden. As he approached a border with Bibles in plain sight, he prayed that the God who made blind eyes see would make seeing eyes blind. The guards waved him through. God can open any closed door.

Brother Lawrence was a humble lay brother who worked in a monastery kitchen in Paris. He learned to talk with God while washing pots, as naturally as in prayer. His letters became The Practice of the Presence of God. The Lord is just as near at the kitchen sink as in the sanctuary.

As a young man, Brother Lawrence looked at a bare tree in winter and realized that it would soon be green again with leaves and fruit. That simple sight gave him a deep sense of God's power and care. The God who brings spring to bare branches can bring new life to a weary soul.

Richard Wurmbrand was a Romanian pastor who spent about fourteen years in communist prisons, much of it in solitary confinement. He said he would sometimes dance for joy in his cell. After his release he founded The Voice of the Martyrs. Christ's presence fills even the loneliest cell.

Sundar Singh grew up in a devout Sikh home in India. As a troubled teenager he burned a Bible in anger, then prayed one night for God to reveal Himself. He said Jesus appeared to him before dawn. He became a wandering preacher in simple robes. Christ answers the honest, searching heart.

William Carey was a poor English shoemaker who taught himself several languages. He urged the church to take the gospel overseas and went to India himself, where he translated the Bible into many languages. He said to expect great things from God and attempt great things for God. God uses humble beginnings.

In eighteen twelve a fire swept through William Carey's printing works in India and destroyed years of translation work. Rather than quit, he and his team started over and redid the work, some of it better than before. God can rebuild what has burned, sometimes better than it was.

Mary Slessor grew up working in a Scottish mill. She went to Calabar in West Africa as a missionary and rescued twins, who in that region were often left to die. She adopted many children herself. The love of God crosses every barrier to rescue those who have been cast aside.

John Paton grew up in a small Scottish cottage where his father would go into a little room to pray. John said he could hear his father pleading for the family. Later John took the gospel to the New Hebrides in the South Pacific. A father's prayers can echo across the oceans.

Mary Jones was a poor Welsh girl who saved for years to buy her own Bible. Around eighteen hundred, she walked many miles barefoot to the town of Bala to get one from Thomas Charles. Her story helped inspire the founding of the British and Foreign Bible Society. God honors hunger for His Word.

Kenneth Taylor wanted his children to understand the Bible during family devotions. So he began paraphrasing it into simple English while riding the commuter train to work in Chicago. That became The Living Bible, read by millions. God's Word was meant to be understood by everyone.

Cameron Townsend was selling Spanish Bibles in Guatemala when a man asked him why, if his God was so great, He did not speak the man's language. Townsend spent years translating the Bible into that language, then founded Wycliffe Bible Translators. God wants to speak to every heart in its own tongue.

Helen Roseveare, a missionary doctor in Africa, told of an orphaned newborn who needed warmth, and a little girl who prayed for a hot water bottle. That same day a parcel arrived, sent months earlier, with a hot water bottle inside, and a doll. God answers prayers before we pray them.

Helen Roseveare was captured and badly mistreated during the civil war in the Congo in the sixties. Later she spoke of sensing God asking whether she would thank Him for trusting her with that suffering. She chose to trust Him and went back to serve. God's grace reaches into the darkest places.

Darlene Deibler Rose was held in a Japanese prison camp during the war. Starving and longing for a banana, she told the Lord she was not asking for one. Soon a guard brought her a whole bunch of bananas. She said God knew exactly what she wanted. The Father knows the desires we hardly dare to speak.

Jackie Pullinger went to Hong Kong as a young Englishwoman with no mission board. She began working in the crowded Walled City among drug addicts and gang members. Many came to Christ and were freed from heroin. God sends the willing to the hardest places and works wonders there.

Bethany Hamilton was a thirteen year old surfer in Hawaii when a shark took her left arm. She clung to her faith and was back on her surfboard within weeks. She went on to compete professionally and to encourage others. God can give courage that is stronger than fear.

Nick Vujicic was born in Australia without arms or legs and as a boy wondered why God had made him that way. As a teenager he read about the man born blind in John chapter nine and found hope. He now travels the world sharing Christ. God has a purpose for every life He makes.

Jim Cymbala pastored a small, struggling church in Brooklyn. When his teenage daughter wandered far from God, the church prayed for her one Tuesday night. Within days she came home and knelt before her father, asking forgiveness. The Lord hears a praying church, and prodigals still come home.

Dietrich Bonhoeffer was a German pastor imprisoned during the Second World War. From his cell he wrote letters and a poem about being kept by good powers through the night. He was executed shortly before the war ended. Even in prison, God's presence surrounded him with peace.

Susanna Wesley had many children and little privacy. When she needed time to pray, she would pull her apron over her head, and her children knew not to disturb her. Two of her sons, John and Charles, changed the world for Christ. God meets a busy mother in her quiet moments.

On a stormy voyage to Georgia in seventeen thirty six, John Wesley was terrified as the waves crashed over the ship. He noticed a group of Moravian Christians calmly singing hymns, even the children, unafraid to die. That calm stayed with him for life. Peace in the storm is a witness of God's care.

C. S. Lewis married Joy Davidman late in life, and soon she was dying of cancer. After she died, he wrote A Grief Observed, honestly describing his pain and doubts. In time he found his footing again in God. The Lord is patient with our grief and does not leave us in it.

Sabine Baring Gould was a young curate in Yorkshire who needed a song for the children to sing as they marched to a neighboring village. In one evening he wrote Onward, Christian Soldiers. Children have sung it for generations. God can use a quick, simple song for lasting good.

Jonathan Edwards, a pastor in colonial New England, described walking alone in his father's pasture as a young man and being filled with a sweet sense of God's glory in the sky, the clouds, and the grass. Creation itself became a window to God's beauty. The heavens still declare His glory.

David Brainerd was a young missionary to Native Americans in the seventeen forties, sick with tuberculosis. He prayed for hours in the snowy woods. His diary, published after his early death, inspired generations of missionaries. A short life poured out in prayer can bear fruit for centuries.

Lilias Trotter was a gifted young artist whom the famous critic John Ruskin wanted to train. She chose instead to go to Algeria as a missionary, where she served for about forty years. She still painted, sketching flowers and desert scenes. God gives back beauty to those who lay their gifts down for Him.

Lottie Moon served as a missionary in China for almost forty years. She wrote letters home urging churches to give and pray. During a famine, she shared her own food with those around her and grew very weak. Her letters still inspire giving each Christmas. Love gives until it costs something.

Ida Scudder was a missionary's daughter in India who did not want to be a missionary. One night three young women died in childbirth because no woman doctor was available. She studied medicine and founded a hospital in Vellore. God can turn one heartbreaking night into a lifetime of healing.

Bilquis Sheikh was a wealthy Muslim woman in Pakistan who began reading the Bible and dreaming of Jesus. A missionary told her to pray to God as her Father. She did, and came to faith, though it cost her family and position. Her book was called I Dared to Call Him Father. God welcomes those who seek Him.

Samuel Crowther was rescued from a slave ship as a boy in West Africa. He came to faith, became a scholar, and was later made the first African Anglican bishop, helping translate the Bible into Yoruba. God can lift a captive child into a life of freedom and service.

Watchman Nee was a Chinese church leader who wrote many books on the Christian life. He spent about the last twenty years of his life in prison for his faith. After he died, a note was found by his bed saying that Christ is the Son of God who died for sinners and rose again. Faith outlasted the prison.

Wang Mingdao was a Chinese pastor who spent more than twenty years in prison for refusing to bend his faith. When finally released as an old man, he still spoke of God's faithfulness. The Lord keeps His own through long years that seem to have no end.

Pandita Ramabai was an Indian scholar and widow who searched many religions for peace. She came to faith in Christ and opened homes for widows and orphaned girls, caring for thousands. She also translated the Bible into Marathi. The love of Jesus gives dignity to those the world overlooks.

Gladys Staines lost her husband Graham and two young sons when they were killed in India in nineteen ninety nine. She publicly forgave the killers and stayed to continue caring for leprosy patients. Her forgiveness amazed the nation. God's grace makes forgiveness possible when it seems impossible.

Steve Saint's father was one of five missionaries killed in Ecuador in nineteen fifty six. As a grown man, Steve became close friends with Mincaye, one of the men who had killed his father, and who later came to faith. Mincaye became like a grandfather to his children. Only God could write such a story.

Florence Nightingale wrote that at sixteen she sensed God calling her to His service, though she did not yet know how. Years later she nursed wounded soldiers by lamplight and reshaped nursing itself. God plants a calling early and unfolds it patiently over many years.

Orel Hershiser, the baseball pitcher, was asked on a late night television show in nineteen eighty eight what he sang to himself to stay calm on the mound. He quietly sang the Doxology, praise God from whom all blessings flow. God can be praised on any stage, even a talk show.

Haldor Lillenas wrote Wonderful Grace of Jesus while pastoring a small church in Illinois early in the last century, with very little money to his name. The song has been sung joyfully ever since. God's grace is greater than all our sin and greater than every lack.

Audrey Mieir was at a Christmas service in nineteen fifty nine when the phrase His name is wonderful caught her heart. She soon set it to music, and it became a favorite in many churches. A moment of worship can become a gift for countless others. God loves to be worshiped by name.

Vestal Goodman sang gospel music with her husband's family for decades, waving a handkerchief as she sang. Even through health problems, she kept singing until near the end of her life, including at the Gaither Homecomings. God's faithfulness gives the old saints a song that lasts.

Jake Hess was a beloved gospel singer known for his warm, expressive voice. Through serious heart trouble in his later years, he kept singing about heaven at the Gaither Homecomings. God gives His people songs of heaven to carry them home. The old songs grow sweeter near the finish line.

B. J. Thomas had hit records like Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head but was trapped by drug addiction. In the mid seventies he came to faith in Christ and was freed. He went on to record gospel albums and won Grammy awards for them. Jesus can break the chains that fame cannot.

Matthew Ward of Second Chapter of Acts was only a boy when he began singing with his sisters after his parents died. He went on to sing for decades with a strong, clear voice. God's care for orphans is not just a promise in the Bible but a story He keeps writing in families.

Larnelle Harris grew up in Kentucky and became one of gospel music's most loved voices in the eighties, singing songs like I Miss My Time with You. That song reminded listeners that the Lord longs for our company. God desires time with His children, even in the middle of busy lives.

The Speer Family were one of the early Southern gospel family groups, singing for generations from the twenties onward and passing songs from parents to children. Families who sing together about the Lord leave a heritage. God's faithfulness flows from one generation to the next.

John Newton wrote the hymn Glorious Things of Thee Are Spoken as well as Amazing Grace. Late in life, when his memory was failing, he said there were two things he still remembered. That he was a great sinner, and that Christ was a great Savior. God's grace is the last thing a soul forgets.

Corrie's watchmaker father taught her to trust God's timing using the image of a train ticket. You are given the ticket just before you board, not weeks before. So God gives strength just when it is needed. Such grace for each moment comes from a Father who never hands it out too early or too late.

John Bunyan's blind daughter Mary used to bring him soup while he was in jail. He said parting from her was like pulling the flesh from his bones. Yet he trusted God with his family. The Father cares for those we love when we cannot be with them ourselves.

Elisabeth Elliot, later in life, lost her second husband Addison Leitch to cancer after only a few years of marriage. She went on to teach and write about trusting God. She often told people to do the next thing. The Lord gives grace enough to take one quiet step at a time.

Ira Sankey, in his later years, became blind. Old friends would visit and sing with him the songs he had once led for crowds of thousands. He died in eighteen ninety eight. A voice that once filled great halls ended quietly in the dark, still trusting. God keeps His singers to the very end.

D. L. Moody once arrived at a meeting in Scotland, and a man named Henry Varley had told him the world has yet to see what God will do with a man fully consecrated to Him. Moody resolved to be that man. God delights to use a heart fully given over to Him, whoever that person is.

Reginald Heber was a vicar in England who wrote Holy, Holy, Holy for Trinity Sunday. He later went to India as a bishop and died there after only a few years. His hymn has been sung in churches around the world. God's holiness is worth a whole life of worship.

Thomas Chisholm lived into his nineties, spending his last years in a Methodist home for retired ministers in New Jersey. By then Great Is Thy Faithfulness was loved around the world, helped along by Billy Graham's crusades. God's faithfulness carried him from youth to old age.

Robert Lowry was a Baptist pastor who wrote both words and music. One hot afternoon in Brooklyn, thinking about the river of life in heaven, he wrote Shall We Gather at the River. God's people will one day gather by that beautiful river, where there is no more sorrow.

William Bradbury composed the music for Jesus Loves Me in eighteen sixty two, setting the Warner sisters' poem to a simple tune. Millions of children have learned their first song about God from it. God's love is the first and last song His children need to know.

Katharina von Schlegel, a German woman of the seventeen hundreds, wrote Be Still, My Soul. Little is known about her life, but her hymn has given peace to the grieving for centuries. A quiet saint whose name is almost forgotten can still comfort millions. God remembers every faithful heart.

Mosie Lister was a Southern gospel songwriter who wrote Till the Storm Passes By, a song asking the Lord to hide us in His hand until the storm is over. Many have sung it through hard nights. God gives shelter in the storm and holds His children close until it passes.

Ray Palmer was a young teacher in New York, not yet twenty two, when he wrote My Faith Looks Up to Thee in a little notebook. He later said he wrote it with tears. Lowell Mason found it and set it to music. A private prayer written in tears can become a hymn for the whole church.

Eliza Hewitt was a schoolteacher in Philadelphia who suffered a serious back injury and spent a long season confined to bed. During her recovery she wrote cheerful hymns like Sunshine in My Soul. God can bring brightness into a sickroom and turn long confinement into a season of song.

Helen Lemmel was a singer whose husband left her after she went blind. In her grief she read a tract that urged readers to turn their eyes upon Jesus. She wrote that phrase into a hymn. When we look full in His wonderful face, the things of earth grow strangely dim.

Samuel Stone wrote The Church's One Foundation in eighteen sixty six, a time of division in the church. He wanted to remind believers that Jesus Christ is the one foundation. Through every storm and quarrel, the church stands on Christ alone. He holds His people together.

Edward Hopper was a pastor to sailors in New York harbor. He wrote Jesus, Savior, Pilot Me for the seamen who came to his church. Many a sailor found comfort in it on rough seas. The Lord is the pilot who guides us safely through every storm to the other shore.

Folliott Pierpoint was walking near the city of Bath in England on a lovely spring day, looking out at the countryside. He wrote For the Beauty of the Earth in gratitude. God is behind every beauty we see, from sky to field. Every good and perfect gift comes from the Father of lights.

Henry van Dyke was a pastor and professor who was visiting Williams College in the Berkshire mountains. Inspired by the hills, he wrote Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee to Beethoven's Ode to Joy. Joy in God is the deepest joy there is, and creation joins the song.

Ira Stanphill was a pastor and songwriter who wrote Mansion over the Hilltop and Room at the Cross for You. He wrote many songs from his own sorrows and pastoral work. There is always room at the cross. God never turns anyone away who comes to Him.

Esther Kerr Rusthoi wrote When We See Christ, a song promising that it will be worth it all when we see Jesus. It has comforted many who are tired of the road. One glimpse of His dear face will make all sorrow fade. God's promise of heaven puts present troubles in perspective.

Johnson Oatman wrote Count Your Blessings, encouraging tired people to name their blessings one by one. He was a businessman and lay preacher who wrote thousands of gospel songs. Counting blessings at night is a cure for worry. God's gifts are more than we can number.

Cecil Frances Alexander wrote hymns to help children understand the Apostles' Creed, including There Is a Green Hill Far Away and All Things Bright and Beautiful. She was the wife of an Irish bishop and spent much time visiting the poor. God's truths are meant for children too.

Lelia Morris was a busy mother in Ohio who began writing hymns while doing housework. When her eyesight failed in later life, her son built her a large blackboard so she could still write. She wrote Nearer, Still Nearer. God gives new ways to serve Him as old ways close.

Elisha Hoffman was a pastor who visited a woman overwhelmed with sorrow. He told her to take it all to Jesus. She cried out that she must tell Jesus. That inspired his hymn I Must Tell Jesus. The Lord is always willing to hear our troubles, whatever the hour of night.

Haldor Lillenas and Bertha, his wife, were both songwriters. Haldor wrote over four thousand songs. Bertha wrote songs too. Together they served the Lord through music for decades. God gives couples a shared calling, and He blesses a marriage that sings His praise together.

Daniel Whittle was a soldier in the Civil War who lost an arm. While recovering in a hospital, he found a New Testament his mother had packed and came to faith. He later wrote hymns like I Know Whom I Have Believed. God's Word, quietly packed by a mother, can find a soldier at the right time.

Phillip Bliss wrote Hold the Fort after hearing D. W. Whittle tell a story from the Civil War about soldiers holding a fort until help came. The song became popular at revival meetings. Christ is coming, and His people can hold on until He does. God never abandons His own.

William Doane was a businessman and inventor who also composed hymn tunes. He worked with Fanny Crosby on many songs, including Rescue the Perishing and To God Be the Glory. God gives different gifts to different people, and together they serve Him. The business mind and the poet's heart can unite.

Fanny Crosby spent many evenings visiting the poor in New York's rescue missions. One night she spoke to a young man who needed hope, and he came to faith. She wrote Rescue the Perishing after that night. God sees every soul in the shadows and sends someone to reach them.

Helen Steiner Rice lost her husband during the hard years of the Depression. She went on to write simple verses of faith for greeting cards that comforted millions of people in sickness and sorrow. God can use a few plain lines on a card to lift a heavy heart.

Hannah Whitall Smith wrote The Christian's Secret of a Happy Life, and she knew sorrow herself, having buried several of her children. She learned to rest her full weight on God's promises. The Lord's secret is not a method but a Person who keeps us in perfect peace.

Oswald Chambers served as a chaplain to soldiers in Egypt during the First World War, giving talks in a simple hut. He died there suddenly. His wife Biddy later gathered her shorthand notes of his talks into My Utmost for His Highest, still read every day. God multiplies a faithful wife's quiet work.

Andrew Murray was a South African pastor who lost his voice for two years. During that silence, he learned deeper dependence on God and later wrote about humility and prayer. God can speak most clearly to us when He quiets our own voices. Silence can become a school of grace.

Evie Tornquist was a young Norwegian American singer who was much loved in Christian music in the seventies. Her gentle song Give Them All to Jesus encouraged listeners to hand over their broken dreams and worries. God takes what we surrender and gives back something better.

Gloria Gaither has said that many of the songs she wrote with Bill grew out of ordinary family life, raising children and walking through seasons of doubt and hope. Their songs feel like home to many listeners for that reason. God meets us in the everyday places of family life.

Bill and Gloria Gaither wrote Something Beautiful about the way God takes our brokenness and confusion and makes something lovely out of it. Many people who felt their lives were ruined have found hope in that simple song. God is still in the business of making broken things beautiful.

The Gaither Vocal Band began in the early eighties, with Bill Gaither and various singers over the years. Their warm harmonies helped carry old hymns and new gospel songs to younger listeners. God keeps the old songs alive by placing them in new voices, generation after generation.

George Younce sang bass with the Cathedrals Quartet for decades. Even when his health failed and he needed dialysis, he still sang at the Gaither Homecomings, often from a chair. God gives strength to finish well, and a joyful heart outlasts a failing body.

Glen Payne sang lead with the Cathedrals for decades. Dying of cancer in nineteen ninety nine, he joined the National Quartet Convention by telephone from his hospital bed and sang I Won't Have to Cross Jordan Alone. The crowd stood. God gives songs of hope to the very end.

Squire Parsons was a music teacher who wrote Beulah Land in the early seventies. That longing song about the land of rest became one of the best known gospel songs of its era. God plants a homesickness for heaven in His children, and He will bring them safely home.

Rusty Goodman sang with his family, the Happy Goodmans, and wrote Who Am I, a song marveling that the King would die for someone like him. He died of cancer in nineteen ninety. The grace that amazed him carried him home. God loves the undeserving, and that never gets old.

The Imperials began in the sixties as a gospel quartet and later backed Elvis Presley in concerts. They then moved toward contemporary Christian music in the seventies, bringing the gospel to a new generation. God can use one group to bridge many styles and reach many hearts.

Dallas Holm wrote Rise Again in the late seventies, a song sung from the point of view of Jesus promising resurrection. It became one of the most popular Christian songs of that era. The promise of resurrection is the heart of the gospel. Because He rose, we will rise too.

Don Francisco wrote He's Alive, a song telling the resurrection morning through the eyes of Peter. Many listeners heard the Easter story fresh through that song. God's story never grows old. The empty tomb still brings hope to every grieving and doubting heart.

Russ Taff sang with The Imperials and later as a solo artist. He has spoken openly about his long struggle with alcoholism and how God brought him through recovery. God's grace does not give up on us when we fall, and He lifts us up again and again.

Cynthia Clawson recorded Softly and Tenderly and other hymns with a voice that many found deeply comforting. She has spent her life singing the old hymns. The Lord calls softly and tenderly to the weary, inviting them home. His voice is gentle, and His door is always open.

The Cathedrals Quartet sang together from the sixties to nineteen ninety nine. When they retired, many fans grieved. Yet their recordings still play on radio stations at night. God's music outlives the singers. The songs of faith keep comforting long after the final concert.

Jim Hill wrote What a Day That Will Be in the fifties. He was a gospel singer in Ohio. The song looks forward to the day when there will be no more sorrow or pain. God's promise of heaven has been a comfort to millions of grieving hearts through that simple, gentle song.

Ira Sankey and D. L. Moody held meetings across Britain in the eighteen seventies. Sankey would sit at a small organ and sing solos, and crowds hushed to listen. Many came to faith through a single song. God uses music to soften hard hearts and open them to the gospel.
reference: Ira Sankey and D. L. Moody

content: Katherine Hankey was an Englishwoman who taught Bible classes for young women in London. During a long illness she wrote a poem about the old, old story of Jesus and His love. It became the hymn I Love to Tell the Story. God's oldest story is always new to a heart that hears it.

Joseph Gilmore was a young preacher in Philadelphia who spoke on Psalm twenty three. Afterwards, talking with friends about being led by God, he wrote He Leadeth Me on a scrap of paper. His wife sent it to a newspaper without telling him. God leads us, and sometimes others share what we wrote in secret.

Thomas Obadiah Chisholm also wrote Living for Jesus, a hymn about giving a whole life to the Lord. He wrote over a thousand poems during his long life. God does not need dramatic people. He uses steady, faithful hearts who simply keep writing and serving year after year.

Lewis Edgar Jones wrote There Is Power in the Blood at a camp meeting in Virginia in the eighteen hundreds. That song has rung out in churches for generations. God's power to cleanse and heal comes through the cross of Jesus. Nothing else can wash away sin.

Elvina Hall was sitting in the choir loft during a long sermon in Baltimore and wrote the words to Jesus Paid It All in the flyleaf of her hymnal. The church organist happened to have a tune that fit perfectly. God can work even through a wandering mind in church.

Phoebe Knapp, a friend of Fanny Crosby, wrote the melody for Blessed Assurance. She was a woman of means who opened her home for music and ministry. God gives some people wealth and gifts so they can bless others through song and hospitality.

Lowell Mason was a banker who loved music. He composed tunes for hymns like Nearer, My God, to Thee and My Faith Looks Up to Thee. He also helped bring music education into American schools. God uses a banker's love of music to lift the hearts of generations.

Sarah Flower Adams wrote Nearer, My God, to Thee in eighteen forty one, based on Jacob's dream at Bethel. Her own health was frail, and she died young. The hymn has been sung at many funerals and in many hard moments. God draws near to us even when the road is rough and dark.

George Duffield heard the dying words of a young pastor friend, Dudley Tyng, who urged believers to stand up for Jesus. The next Sunday Duffield preached on that theme and wrote Stand Up, Stand Up for Jesus. God can turn a friend's last words into a call heard by thousands.

A man blind from birth sat begging in Jerusalem. Jesus spat on the ground, made mud, put it on his eyes, and told him to wash in the pool of Siloam. He went, washed, and came back seeing. Jesus shows that no darkness is too old or too deep for His light to reach.

Questioned again and again by the religious leaders, the man who had been born blind would not argue theology. He simply said that one thing he knew, that he was blind and now he could see. Sometimes the plainest testimony is the strongest. God's work in a life speaks for itself.

Thrown out of the synagogue for speaking up about his healing, the formerly blind man found himself alone. Then Jesus went looking for him, revealed Himself as the Son of Man, and the man worshiped Him. When others push us out, the Good Shepherd comes to find us.

Four friends carried a paralyzed man to a crowded house where Jesus was teaching. Unable to get through the door, they opened up the roof and lowered him down. Jesus saw their faith, forgave his sins, and told him to get up and walk. God honors the faith of friends who carry us.

A Roman centurion's servant was sick and near death. The officer sent word to Jesus, saying he was not worthy to have Him under his roof, but if Jesus would only say the word, his servant would be healed. Jesus marveled at his faith, and the servant was well. God's word reaches across any distance.

Near the town of Nain, Jesus met a funeral procession. A widow was burying her only son. Moved with compassion, Jesus told her not to weep, touched the bier, and told the young man to arise. He sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him back to his mother. The Lord sees a mother's grief.

Jairus, a synagogue ruler, fell at Jesus' feet and begged Him to come, because his little daughter was dying. On the way, word came that she had died. Jesus told him, do not be afraid, only believe. God's timing may feel late to us, but it is never too late for Him.

At Jairus' house, the mourners laughed when Jesus said the girl was only sleeping. He took her by the hand and said, little girl, arise. She got up and walked, and He told them to give her something to eat. The Lord of life is also tender about a child's supper.

When Lazarus fell sick, Jesus waited two more days before going to Bethany. By the time He arrived, Lazarus had been in the tomb four days. Standing with the grieving sisters, Jesus wept. Our Savior does not stand aloof from sorrow. He enters into it and weeps with us.

Jesus stood at the tomb of Lazarus and called in a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. The man who had died walked out, still wrapped in grave clothes. Jesus told them to unbind him and let him go. The One who is the resurrection and the life will one day call all His own from the grave.

Martha met Jesus on the road after her brother died, grieving and honest. When He asked if she believed He was the resurrection and the life, she said yes, Lord, I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God. Faith can speak clearly even through tears. God meets us in our grief.

While Martha was busy in the kitchen, her sister Mary sat at Jesus' feet, listening. When Martha complained, Jesus gently said that Mary had chosen the good part, which would not be taken away. God values our presence with Him even more than our service for Him.

Six days before the Passover, Mary of Bethany poured costly perfume on Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair. The whole house filled with the fragrance. When some objected to the cost, Jesus defended her. Love given to Jesus is never wasted, and He receives it gladly.

A Gentile woman from the region of Tyre begged Jesus to heal her daughter. When He tested her, she answered humbly that even the dogs eat the crumbs under the table. Jesus praised her answer, and her daughter was healed. God rewards persistent, humble faith.

Some people brought Jesus a man who was deaf and could hardly speak. Jesus took him aside from the crowd, touched his ears and tongue, looked up to heaven, sighed, and said Ephphatha, be opened. At once he could hear and speak plainly. The Lord deals with each of us personally and gently.

At Bethsaida, Jesus led a blind man out of the village and touched his eyes. At first the man saw people like trees walking. Jesus touched him again, and he saw everything clearly. Sometimes God's healing comes in stages, but He always finishes what He begins.

For thirty eight years a man had been sick, lying by the pool of Bethesda with no one to help him into the water. Jesus asked if he wanted to be made well, then told him to rise, take up his bed, and walk. He did. No wait is too long for Jesus to end.

A royal official from Capernaum begged Jesus to come before his son died. Jesus told him to go his way, his son would live. The man believed the word and went home. His servants met him on the road to say the boy had recovered at that very hour. God's word is enough to trust.

In a synagogue on the Sabbath, a woman had been bent over for eighteen years and could not straighten up. Jesus called her over, laid His hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God. The Lord sees those bowed low and lifts them up.

A man with a leprous body came to Jesus, knelt, and said, if You are willing, You can make me clean. Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out and touched him, saying, I am willing, be clean. The Lord does not keep the hurting at arm's length. He touches the untouchable.

Peter's mother in law lay sick with a fever. Jesus came into the house, took her by the hand, and lifted her up. The fever left her at once, and she got up and served them. Christ's healing gives back not only health but purpose, a way to serve again.

In the synagogue a man with a withered hand stood before Jesus while critics watched closely. Jesus told him to stretch out his hand, and it was restored, whole like the other. God's mercy is not limited by the rules people make. He delights to restore.

Two blind men followed Jesus, crying out for mercy. He asked if they believed He was able to do this, and they said yes, Lord. He touched their eyes and said, according to your faith let it be to you. Their eyes were opened. God responds to simple faith in His power.

On the night Jesus was arrested, Peter drew a sword and cut off the right ear of Malchus, the high priest's servant. Jesus said, permit even this, touched the man's ear, and healed him. Even at His own arrest, Jesus showed mercy to those who came against Him.

A great crowd followed Jesus to a remote hillside, and evening came with nothing to eat. A boy had five barley loaves and two small fish. Jesus gave thanks, and thousands ate until they were full, with baskets left over. God multiplies small offerings beyond imagining.

After a long night of catching nothing, Simon Peter let down his nets again because Jesus said so. The nets filled until they began to break. Peter fell at Jesus' knees and said he was a sinful man. Jesus told him not to fear, from now on he would catch people. God calls us right where we work.

Late in the night, in the fourth watch, the disciples saw Jesus walking on the sea. Peter asked to come to Him and stepped out of the boat. When he saw the wind he began to sink and cried, Lord, save me. Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and caught him. The Lord catches us when we falter.

Jesus was asleep in the stern of the boat on a cushion when a great storm arose. The frightened disciples woke Him. He rebuked the wind and said to the sea, peace, be still. There was a great calm. The One who can sleep in the storm can also speak peace to it.

Thomas would not believe the others had seen the risen Lord unless he could touch His wounds. Eight days later Jesus appeared and invited him to do just that. Thomas answered, my Lord and my God. Jesus meets honest doubt with patience and turns it into worship.

Two disciples walked to Emmaus, downcast after the crucifixion. A stranger joined them and explained the scriptures about the Messiah. At supper, when He broke the bread, their eyes were opened and they knew it was Jesus. He walks beside discouraged hearts long before they recognize Him.

After Jesus vanished from the table at Emmaus, the two disciples said to each other, did not our hearts burn within us while He talked with us on the road? That very hour they hurried back to Jerusalem in the dark. When the Lord warms a heart, it cannot keep the news to itself.

Simeon was an old, devout man in Jerusalem who had been promised he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ. When Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus to the temple, Simeon took Him in his arms and blessed God. Now he could depart in peace. God keeps His promises to the patient.

Anna was a prophetess, a widow for many years, who never left the temple but worshiped there night and day with fasting and prayer. When she saw the infant Jesus, she gave thanks and spoke of Him to all who waited for redemption. God rewards a lifetime of faithful waiting.

Zechariah, an old priest, was told by an angel in the temple that his wife Elizabeth would bear a son. He doubted and was made unable to speak until the promise came true. When John was born, his tongue was freed and he praised God. The Lord is faithful even when we struggle to believe.

Elizabeth had lived with the sorrow of childlessness into old age. When she conceived, she said the Lord had looked on her and taken away her reproach. Later her baby leaped within her at Mary's greeting. God's timing can turn a long sorrow into overflowing joy.

A young woman named Mary was told by the angel Gabriel that she would bear the Son of God. She asked how this could be, and the angel said nothing will be impossible with God. Mary answered, behold the maidservant of the Lord, let it be to me according to your word. God honors surrendered hearts.

Mary visited her cousin Elizabeth and burst into a song of praise. She said her soul magnified the Lord, who had regarded the lowly state of His servant and filled the hungry with good things. God lifts up the humble and remembers His mercy.

Joseph was a righteous man who planned to quietly break his engagement to Mary. But an angel appeared to him in a dream and told him not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife. He awoke and did exactly as told. God guides those who are willing to obey Him.

Shepherds were keeping watch over their flocks by night when an angel appeared and the glory of the Lord shone around them. They were told a Savior was born in Bethlehem. They hurried to find Him, then returned glorifying God. God's good news first came to ordinary workers on the night shift.

Wise men from the east followed a star to find the newborn King. When the star stopped over the place where the child was, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy. They worshiped Him and offered gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh. God leads seekers to His Son.

Warned in a dream that Herod would seek the child's life, Joseph rose by night, took the young Child and His mother, and fled to Egypt. They stayed until Herod died. God protects His own, sometimes by quiet journeys in the dark, guided step by step.

When Jesus was twelve, He stayed behind at the temple after Passover. Mary and Joseph searched for three days before finding Him among the teachers. Mary kept all these things in her heart. Some of God's ways we cannot yet understand, but we can treasure them and wait.

At a wedding in Cana, the wine ran out. Mary told the servants, whatever He says to you, do it. Jesus had them fill jars with water, and when they drew it out, it was fine wine. God's first sign was at a family celebration. He cares about our joys as well as our sorrows.

John the Baptist, sitting in Herod's prison, sent his disciples to ask Jesus if He was really the one to come. Jesus sent back word of the blind seeing, the lame walking, and the poor hearing good news. Even great saints have dark days, and Jesus answers them gently.

Andrew heard John the Baptist call Jesus the Lamb of God and spent the day with Him. The first thing Andrew did was find his brother Simon and tell him they had found the Messiah. Then he brought him to Jesus. God often works through one person bringing another.

Jesus saw a poor widow drop two small copper coins into the temple treasury. He told His disciples that she had given more than all the others, because she gave all she had to live on. God measures a gift not by its size but by the heart behind it.

People brought little children to Jesus so He might touch them, and the disciples tried to send them away. Jesus was displeased and said, let the little children come to Me. He took them up in His arms and blessed them. Jesus always has time for the little ones.

Simon of Cyrene was coming in from the country when soldiers forced him to carry Jesus' cross. He did not ask for it, yet he walked behind the Savior on the way to Golgotha. Mark names his sons, which suggests his family was known to the church. God can use an unplanned moment for lasting good.

Joseph of Arimathea was a member of the council and a secret disciple of Jesus. After the crucifixion, he took courage and asked Pilate for the body. He laid Jesus in his own new tomb cut from rock. God gives courage to quiet believers when the moment calls for it.

Simon Peter answered Jesus' question, who do you say that I am, with the words, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus told him that flesh and blood had not revealed this, but His Father in heaven. Faith in Christ is a gift God reveals to the heart.

Weeks after denying Jesus, Peter stood before a crowd in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost and boldly preached that God had raised Jesus from the dead. About three thousand people believed and were baptized. God can turn a frightened man into a fearless witness.

Every day a man lame from birth was carried to the temple gate called Beautiful to beg. Peter said he had no silver or gold, but in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk. The man leaped up, walking and praising God. Jesus gives far more than we ask.

When Peter and John were ordered to stop speaking about Jesus, they answered that they could not help speaking about what they had seen and heard. The rulers marveled that these uneducated men had been with Jesus. God gives boldness to ordinary people.

Stephen was full of faith and the Holy Spirit. As he was being stoned for his witness, he looked up and saw the heavens opened and Jesus standing at God's right hand. He prayed for those killing him and fell asleep. God's presence is nearest when the cost is highest.

Barnabas, whose name means son of encouragement, sold a field he owned and laid the money at the apostles' feet. He gave freely to help those in need. God loves a cheerful giver, and He uses generous hearts to care for His people.

When Saul came to Jerusalem after his conversion, the disciples were afraid of him. But Barnabas took him, brought him to the apostles, and told them how Saul had seen the Lord and preached boldly. God uses encouragers to open doors for new believers.

The Lord spoke in a vision to a disciple named Ananias, telling him to go and lay hands on Saul, the man known for persecuting believers. Ananias was afraid but obeyed, calling him brother Saul. God asks His people to welcome even those they once feared.

In Joppa, a disciple named Tabitha, also called Dorcas, was full of good works and charity, sewing clothes for widows. When she died, the widows wept and showed Peter the garments. Peter prayed, and she opened her eyes. God sees every quiet act of kindness.

In Lydda, Peter found a man named Aeneas who had been bedridden for eight years with paralysis. Peter said, Aeneas, Jesus the Christ heals you. Arise and make your bed. He arose immediately, and many turned to the Lord. God works through His servants to show His power.

Peter was asleep in prison between two soldiers, bound with chains, the night before his trial. An angel woke him, the chains fell off, and the iron gate opened by itself. Peter could sleep because he trusted God. The Lord can bring His people out of any prison.

When Peter knocked at the gate after his escape from prison, a servant girl named Rhoda recognized his voice. She was so glad that she ran in to tell the others without opening the gate. They thought she was out of her mind. God sometimes answers prayers so quickly that we can hardly believe it.

While the believers were praying for Peter in prison, the church prayed without ceasing. That very night God sent an angel to deliver him. The answer came while they were still praying. The Lord hears the prayers of His people in the night.

On Cyprus, the Roman proconsul Sergius Paulus, a thoughtful man, wanted to hear the word of God. A sorcerer tried to turn him away, but when the proconsul saw what happened, he believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord. God draws the honest seeker.

In Lystra, a man crippled from birth listened to Paul speaking. Paul saw he had faith to be healed and said loudly, stand up straight on your feet. The man leaped and walked. God sees faith even in someone who has never walked a single step.

At Lystra, Paul was stoned by a mob and dragged out of the city, left for dead. As the disciples gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. The next day he continued his journey. God gives His servants strength to rise and keep going.

Timothy grew up with a mother named Eunice and a grandmother named Lois who both had sincere faith. From childhood he knew the holy scriptures. He became Paul's faithful helper. God uses the faith passed on by mothers and grandmothers to shape the next generation.

In Corinth, Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his household. Many Corinthians also believed and were baptized. One night the Lord told Paul in a vision not to be afraid, for He had many people in that city. God has people waiting to hear.

Priscilla and Aquila were tentmakers who worked alongside Paul. When they heard the gifted preacher Apollos, they invited him home and explained the way of God more accurately. God uses humble couples to quietly strengthen others in the faith.

During a long sermon by Paul late into the night, a young man named Eutychus fell asleep in a window and fell three stories to his death. Paul embraced him, and the young man was brought back alive. The believers were greatly comforted. God's mercy reaches even a drowsy listener.

Paul said farewell to the Ephesian elders, telling them he did not count his life dear to himself, so that he might finish his race with joy. They knelt and prayed together and wept as they walked him to the ship. God gives His servants joy in finishing the course He has set for them.

Caught in a fierce storm for many days, with all hope of being saved gone, Paul stood among the frightened sailors and told them to take heart. An angel had told him that no one would be lost. Every person on board reached land safely. God keeps His promises even in the storm.

After the shipwreck on Malta, Paul gathered sticks for a fire, and a viper fastened on his hand. The islanders expected him to swell up and die. He shook it off into the fire and suffered no harm. God protected Paul so that he could continue His work.

Paul begged the Lord three times to remove a painful thorn in his flesh. God answered that His grace was sufficient, for His strength is made perfect in weakness. Paul learned to boast in his weaknesses so that Christ's power would rest on him. God's grace is enough.

Writing from prison, Paul told the Philippians that he had learned to be content in whatever state he was, whether full or hungry, with much or little. He could do all things through Christ who strengthened him. God gives contentment that circumstances cannot steal.

Epaphroditus traveled to bring help to Paul in prison and became so sick that he nearly died. But God had mercy on him and on Paul too, sparing them sorrow upon sorrow. Paul sent him home to be welcomed with joy. God sees those who risk themselves to serve others.

Onesiphorus often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chains. When he came to Rome, he searched diligently until he found Paul in prison. Paul prayed that the Lord would grant him mercy. God remembers those who seek out the lonely and the imprisoned.

John Mark had once left Paul's mission team, and Paul refused to take him along again. But years later Paul wrote asking for Mark to come, saying he was useful for ministry. God restores those who stumble and gives them a second chance to serve.

Standing before King Agrippa in chains, Paul told how the Lord had sent him to open eyes and turn people from darkness to light. He said he wished all who heard him would become as he was, except for the chains. God gives freedom of heart even to a prisoner.

In Samaria, Philip preached Christ, and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed. There was great joy in that city. God sends His good news to places others overlook, and joy follows wherever Jesus is received.

Noah was a righteous man in a violent and corrupt generation. God told him to build an ark, and Noah did everything just as God commanded. Through the flood, God kept Noah and his family safe. The Lord preserves those who walk with Him, even when the world around them is falling apart.

After the flood, Noah came out of the ark and built an altar to the Lord. God set a rainbow in the clouds as a sign of His covenant never again to destroy the earth by flood. Each rainbow is a reminder that God keeps His word.

Enoch walked with God for three hundred years, and then he was not, for God took him. His life was summed up simply, he walked with God. Hebrews says he pleased God. A quiet daily walk with the Lord is the greatest life of all.

God told Abram to leave his country, his family, and his father's house and go to a land He would show him. Abram went, not knowing where he was going, trusting the promise. God leads us one step at a time when we follow by faith.

One night God brought Abram outside and told him to look toward the heavens and count the stars, if he could. So shall your descendants be, God said. Abram believed the Lord, and it was counted to him as righteousness. The God of the stars keeps His promises.

Sarah laughed when she overheard that she would have a son in her old age. The Lord asked, is anything too hard for the Lord? A year later she held Isaac and said God had made her laugh with joy. The Lord can turn a laugh of doubt into a laugh of delight.

Hagar, a servant, fled into the wilderness, alone and mistreated. The Angel of the Lord found her by a spring of water and spoke to her. She called the Lord the God who sees me. No one is too forgotten or far away for God to see.

Years later, Hagar and her son Ishmael wandered in the wilderness and ran out of water. She set the boy under a bush and sat a distance away, weeping. God heard the boy's voice, opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. God hears the cry of the outcast.

Abraham was asked to offer his son Isaac. As they climbed the mountain, Isaac asked where the lamb was. Abraham said God would provide. At the last moment God stopped him and provided a ram. Abraham called the place The Lord Will Provide. God provides what we need.

Abraham's servant was sent to find a wife for Isaac. He prayed by a well for a clear sign, and before he finished praying, Rebekah came out with her water jar and offered to water his camels. He bowed and worshiped God. The Lord guides those who ask Him.

Jacob was fleeing from his brother and slept outdoors with a stone for a pillow. He dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels going up and down, and the Lord promised to be with him. Jacob woke and said, surely the Lord is in this place, and I did not know it. God meets us in lonely places.

Alone by the Jabbok River at night, Jacob wrestled with a man until daybreak. He would not let go until he was blessed. He was given a new name, Israel, and walked away limping but blessed. God sometimes changes us through long nights of wrestling.

Jacob, afraid to meet his brother Esau after many years, sent gifts ahead and prayed. But Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, and wept with him. God can turn years of fear and estrangement into a reunion of tears and peace.

Joseph was thrown into prison for something he did not do. Yet the Lord was with him and showed him mercy, and the keeper of the prison put him in charge. Even in an unjust prison, God was with Joseph. The Lord does not abandon His children in the dark places.

When the aged Jacob heard that his son Joseph was alive in Egypt, he could not believe it at first. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, his spirit revived. He said it was enough, he would go and see Joseph before he died. God restores what we thought was lost.

Moses' mother hid her baby for three months, then placed him in a basket among the reeds of the Nile. Pharaoh's daughter found him, and his own mother was hired to nurse him. God watched over that little basket and turned a mother's fear into a gift.

Moses was tending sheep in the desert when he saw a bush on fire that was not consumed. God called to him from the bush and sent him to lead Israel out of Egypt. God reveals Himself in unexpected places to ordinary people doing ordinary work.

Moses felt unqualified and said he was not eloquent. God answered, who made man's mouth? Now go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what to say. God does not call the qualified. He qualifies those He calls and goes with them.

Trapped between Pharaoh's army and the Red Sea, the Israelites were terrified. Moses told them, do not be afraid, stand still and see the salvation of the Lord. God parted the sea, and they walked through on dry ground. God makes a way where there is no way.

After crossing the sea, Miriam took a tambourine in her hand and led the women in dancing and singing, sing to the Lord, for He has triumphed gloriously. God's people answer His deliverance with grateful song.

Hungry and complaining in the wilderness, the people needed food. God sent manna each morning, bread from heaven, enough for each day. Those who gathered too much found it spoiled. God gives daily bread, teaching His people to trust Him one day at a time.

As the Amalekites attacked Israel, Moses held up his hands on a hilltop. As long as his hands were up, Israel prevailed. When he grew tired, Aaron and Hur held up his arms until sunset. God uses friends to hold up our weary arms.

Moses asked the Lord to show him His glory. God hid him in a cleft of the rock and covered him with His hand as He passed by, proclaiming Himself merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in goodness. God shelters us as He reveals Himself.

Caleb was one of only two spies who trusted God when Israel feared the giants of Canaan. Forty five years later, at eighty five, he asked for the hill country, saying he was as strong as ever. God rewards wholehearted faithfulness, even in old age.

As Joshua took Moses' place, God told him to be strong and courageous, not to be afraid or dismayed, for the Lord his God would be with him wherever he went. God's presence is the source of courage for every new and daunting task.

As soon as the priests carrying the ark stepped into the flooded Jordan, the waters stopped, and Israel crossed on dry ground. Joshua set up twelve stones as a memorial so the children would ask what they meant. God wants His people to remember His mighty deeds.

Deborah, a prophetess and judge, sat under a palm tree as people came to her for judgment. When Israel was oppressed, she called Barak and promised that God would give victory. Afterward they sang together. God raises up unexpected leaders when His people need them.

Hannah's husband Elkanah could not understand her sorrow. He asked why her heart was grieved and said, am I not better to you than ten sons? Even loving people cannot always fix our pain. God alone can reach the deepest grief.

The boy Samuel was sleeping in the temple at night when he heard a voice calling his name. Three times he ran to Eli. Then Eli understood and told him to say, speak, Lord, for Your servant hears. God still speaks in the quiet of the night to listening hearts.

With the Philistines threatening Israel, Samuel prayed, and the Lord thundered against them. Afterwards Samuel set up a stone and called it Ebenezer, saying, thus far the Lord has helped us. Every day God has brought us through is worth remembering.

Young David was a shepherd when Samuel came to anoint the next king. His brothers were tall and impressive, but the Lord said He looks at the heart, not the outward appearance. David was chosen. God sees what others overlook.

David, a shepherd boy, faced the giant Goliath with only a sling and stones. He said he came in the name of the Lord of hosts. With one stone, the giant fell. God gives victory not by sword or spear, but by His own power.
