King Saul was hunting David in the wilderness. Finding Saul asleep in a cave, David could have killed him. Instead, he cut off a corner of his robe and spared him, refusing to harm the Lord's anointed. God gives grace to show mercy when revenge is easy.

Abigail, a wise woman, hurried to meet David with gifts when her foolish husband insulted him. Her gentle words kept David from shedding blood. David blessed God for sending her. God uses wise and peacemaking voices to keep us from regret.

When David and his men came home to Ziklag to find it burned and their families taken, the men wept until they had no strength left. David was greatly distressed, but he strengthened himself in the Lord his God. God is our strength when every other strength is gone.

After becoming king, David asked if anyone was left from Saul's house to whom he could show kindness. He found Mephibosheth, lame in both feet, and gave him a place at the king's table for life. God's grace seats the weak at His own table.

David danced before the Lord with all his might as the ark was brought into Jerusalem. He did not care what others thought. He was celebrating God's presence among His people. God delights in wholehearted worship.

Elijah hid by the brook Cherith during a drought. Ravens brought him bread and meat each morning and evening, and he drank from the brook. God can provide through the most unlikely messengers. He never forgets His servants.

A widow in Zarephath had only a handful of flour and a little oil. Elijah asked her to make him a small cake first. She did, and her flour and oil did not run out until the rain came. God provides for those who trust Him with the little they have.

Later the widow of Zarephath's son died. Elijah carried the boy upstairs, stretched himself on him three times, and cried to the Lord. The boy revived. Elijah brought him down and said, see, your son lives. God hears desperate prayers and gives life.

On Mount Carmel, Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal. After soaking his altar with water, he prayed a simple prayer. Fire fell from heaven and consumed everything. The people fell on their faces and cried, the Lord, He is God. God answers prayer.

Exhausted and afraid, Elijah lay down under a broom tree and asked to die. An angel touched him and said, arise and eat, because the journey is too great for you. He found bread and water and slept. God's first answer to despair is often rest and nourishment.

On Mount Horeb, Elijah saw a great wind, an earthquake, and a fire, but God was not in them. Then came a still small voice, and Elijah heard God. God often speaks not in the noise but in a gentle whisper in the quiet night.

Obadiah was in charge of King Ahab's household, yet he feared the Lord greatly. When the queen was killing the Lord's prophets, he hid a hundred of them in caves and fed them bread and water. God has faithful people even in unlikely places.

When Elijah was taken up into heaven, Elisha asked for a double portion of his spirit. Elijah's mantle fell, and Elisha picked it up and struck the Jordan, and the waters parted. God's work continues from one generation to the next.

A widow was in debt, and creditors were coming to take her two sons as slaves. She had only a jar of oil. Elisha told her to borrow empty vessels and pour. The oil kept flowing until every jar was full. God's supply fits the size of our faith.

A Shunammite woman made a small room for Elisha on her rooftop. Later, her son died suddenly. She laid him on the prophet's bed and went to find Elisha, saying, it is well. Elisha prayed, and the boy was restored. God honors faith and hospitality.

A young prophet was cutting wood by the Jordan when his borrowed axe head fell into the water. He cried out, alas, it was borrowed. Elisha threw a stick into the water, and the iron floated. God cares even about small worries and borrowed tools.

Elisha's servant woke to find the city surrounded by an enemy army and was terrified. Elisha told him not to fear, for those with us are more than those with them. He prayed, and the servant saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire. God's protection is greater than we see.

When King Hezekiah received a threatening letter from the Assyrian king, he went to the temple and spread it out before the Lord, praying for deliverance. God answered, and Jerusalem was saved. We can bring every frightening letter and lay it before God.

King Hezekiah was sick and told he would die. He turned his face to the wall, prayed, and wept bitterly. God said, I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears, and added fifteen years to his life. God sees our tears and hears our prayers.

Young King Josiah heard the book of the Law read for the first time after it was found in the temple. He tore his clothes in repentance and led the nation to renew their covenant with God. God's Word changes hearts when it is truly heard.

King Jehoshaphat faced a huge army and said, we do not know what to do, but our eyes are upon You. He sent singers ahead of the army praising the beauty of holiness. When they began to sing, God set ambushes against the enemy. God fights for those who look to Him.

Jabez was named in sorrow, yet he called on the God of Israel, asking to be blessed, for God's hand to be with him, and to be kept from evil. And God granted what he asked. God hears the honest prayer of anyone who calls on Him.

Daniel knew the decree against prayer had been signed, yet he went home, opened his windows toward Jerusalem, and prayed three times a day as he always had. When he was thrown to the lions, God shut their mouths. God protects those who stay faithful.

Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refused to bow to the king's golden image. They said God could deliver them, but even if He did not, they would not bow. They were thrown into the furnace, and a fourth figure walked with them in the fire. God is with His people in the fire.

King Nebuchadnezzar became proud and lost his mind, living like an animal in the fields. At the end of that time he lifted his eyes to heaven, his reason returned, and he praised the Most High. God can humble the proud and restore them when they look up.

Daniel prayed and fasted for understanding, confessing his people's sins. While he was still praying, the angel Gabriel came to him and told him that from the first day he set his heart to understand, his words were heard. God hears prayers from the very first word.

Queen Esther had been chosen to be queen of Persia, but now her people faced destruction. Her cousin Mordecai said, who knows whether you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this? She fasted, risked her life, and saved her people. God places us where we are for a purpose.

Nehemiah, the king's cupbearer, heard that Jerusalem's walls lay in ruins. He wept and fasted for days. When the king asked why he was sad, Nehemiah prayed silently to God and then spoke. The king granted his request. God gives favor to those who pray.

When Nehemiah's builders were mocked and threatened, they prayed and set a watch day and night. Half worked while half stood guard. The wall was finished in fifty two days. God strengthens His people to keep building despite opposition.

Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up, and seraphim crying holy, holy, holy. He cried, woe is me, for I am a man of unclean lips. An angel touched his lips with a coal from the altar, and his sin was purged. Then he said, here am I, send me. God cleanses those He calls.

Jeremiah said he was too young to speak. God told him not to say that, for he would go wherever God sent him, and God would put His words in his mouth. God had known him before he was born. God's call comes with God's own help.

Jeremiah was thrown into a muddy cistern and left to sink. Ebed Melech, an Ethiopian servant in the palace, pleaded with the king and pulled Jeremiah out with ropes and old rags so the ropes would not hurt him. God uses kind people to rescue His servants.

While Jerusalem was under siege, God told Jeremiah to buy a field. It seemed foolish, but Jeremiah obeyed, because God promised that houses and fields would again be bought in the land. He prayed, Ah Lord God, nothing is too hard for You. God's promises reach beyond present troubles.

Habakkuk saw troubled times coming, yet he said that though the fig tree may not blossom and there be no fruit on the vines, he would rejoice in the Lord and joy in the God of his salvation. Faith can sing even before the harvest returns.

When the exiles returned and laid the foundation of the new temple, the young people shouted for joy while the old men who remembered the first temple wept aloud. The sounds mingled together. God gives both joy and tears a place in His work.

Barzillai, an old man of eighty, brought food and supplies to David and his weary men when they fled from Absalom. Later David wanted to reward him, but Barzillai asked only to go home and die in his own city, near his parents' grave. God honors quiet kindness and contentment.

After Saul's death, the brave men of Jabesh Gilead walked all night to recover his body and bury it with honor. Years before, Saul had rescued their city. God sees loyalty and gratitude, even in sad and costly acts of kindness done in the dark.

When Israel crossed the Jordan, manna stopped the day after they ate the produce of the land. God had fed them forty years in the wilderness and then provided in a new way. God's provision changes form, but it never stops.

Joanna, the wife of Herod's steward, along with Susanna and many other women, traveled with Jesus after He healed them, and supported Him out of their own means. Their names are written down in scripture. God sees and honors those who quietly support His work.

A scribe asked Jesus which commandment was greatest. Jesus answered to love God with all your heart and your neighbor as yourself. The scribe agreed wholeheartedly, and Jesus told him he was not far from the kingdom of God. God draws near to sincere seekers.

Shiphrah and Puah were Hebrew midwives in Egypt. Pharaoh ordered them to kill the baby boys, but they feared God and let the children live. God dealt well with them and gave them families of their own. The Lord honors those who quietly protect the helpless.

Before he died, Moses climbed Mount Nebo, and the Lord showed him the whole promised land spread out below. Then Moses died there, and the Lord Himself buried him. God's servant ended his long journey in the company of the One he had followed.

Isaac went out to the field one evening to meditate. Lifting his eyes, he saw camels coming, bringing Rebekah. She became his wife, and he loved her, and was comforted after his mother's death. God brings comfort to quiet hearts at evening.

In Egypt, Joseph named his first son Manasseh, saying God had made him forget all his toil, and his second son Ephraim, saying God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction. The Lord can make us fruitful in the very place of our pain.

One night at Gibeon, God appeared to young King Solomon in a dream and said, ask what I shall give you. Solomon asked for an understanding heart to lead the people. God was pleased and gave him wisdom and much more besides. The Lord delights in humble requests.

The Queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's wisdom and came to test him with hard questions. When she saw it all, she said the half had not been told her, and she blessed the Lord his God. God's goodness is always greater than the reports we have heard.

When David was hiding from Saul in the wilderness, Saul's son Jonathan went to find him and strengthened his hand in God. Jonathan reminded David of God's promise. A faithful friend points us back to the Lord when we are weary.

After Elijah prayed on Mount Carmel, he sent his servant seven times to look toward the sea. The seventh time, the servant saw a little cloud like a man's hand rising from the sea. Soon came heavy rain. God answers persistent prayer, often beginning with something small.

When David longed for a drink from the well of Bethlehem, three mighty men broke through enemy lines to bring it. David would not drink it but poured it out to the Lord, because it had been brought at the risk of their lives. God is worthy of our most precious offerings.

King Asa faced a huge army and cried out to the Lord, saying that it was nothing for God to help, whether with many or with those who have no power. He asked God to help, for they rested on Him. The Lord gave victory. God helps those who rest on Him.

Ezekiel was shown a valley full of dry bones. God asked if those bones could live. Ezekiel said, O Lord God, You know. As he spoke God's word, the bones came together and breath entered them, and they stood up. God can bring life to what seems long dead.

The writer of Lamentations sat among the ruins of Jerusalem, weeping. Yet in the middle of his grief he remembered that the Lord's mercies do not fail. They are new every morning. Great is His faithfulness. Hope can rise even in the ashes, because God is faithful.

From the cross, Jesus saw His mother standing near with the disciple whom He loved. He said to her, woman, behold your son, and to the disciple, behold your mother. From that hour the disciple took her into his own home. Even in agony, Jesus cared for His mother.

On the first Easter morning, Peter and John ran together to the tomb. John arrived first, and when he went in and saw the grave clothes lying there, he saw and believed. God's empty tomb turns sorrow into faith.

After being beaten and ordered not to speak in the name of Jesus, the apostles left the council rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name. Daily they kept teaching about Jesus. God gives joy that suffering cannot remove.

When some men plotted to kill Paul in Jerusalem, his young nephew heard of the plan and went into the barracks to warn him. The commander sent Paul away safely under guard that night. God can use a young person's courage to protect His servants.

In Athens, when Paul spoke of the resurrection, some mocked and others wanted to hear more. But a few believed, including Dionysius, a member of the council, and a woman named Damaris. God always has hearts ready to believe, even in a skeptical crowd.

Abraham stood before the Lord and pleaded for the city of Sodom, asking if He would spare it for fifty righteous, then forty five, down to ten. Each time God agreed. The Lord is patient with our prayers and willing to show mercy.

When collectors asked Peter whether Jesus paid the temple tax, Jesus sent Peter to cast a hook into the sea. In the mouth of the first fish he caught, he found a coin enough for both of them. God provides for His children in surprising ways.

Many people brought the sick into the streets of Jerusalem and laid them on beds and mats, hoping that at least Peter's shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by. They were all healed. God worked so powerfully through His church that hope filled the streets.
